components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses and herbs, as in 花, 草, 茶; 苏 originally named the perilla plant, and is also short for Jiangsu and Soviet (苏联).
王 (jade, 斜玉旁) — gems and precious stones, as in 球 ball, 珠 pearl; 珊 is coral.
册 (cè) is a loose clue; 删 shān shares it and sounds exactly like 珊.

example.hanzi: 苏珊是我们班新来的老师。
example.pinyin: Sūshān shì wǒmen bān xīn lái de lǎoshī.
example.english: Susan is the new teacher in our class.
example.fact: The name Susan derives from the Hebrew Shoshanna, meaning 'lily' or 'rose,' by way of Greek and Latin forms. It became one of the most popular English given names for girls in the mid-20th century before falling out of fashion by the 1990s.

examples.hanzi: 苏珊每天骑车去学校。
examples.pinyin: Sūshān měi tiān qí chē qù xuéxiào.
examples.english: Susan rides her bike to school every day.

examples.hanzi: 我昨天给苏珊发了一条短信。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān gěi Sūshān fā le yì tiáo duǎnxìn.
examples.english: I sent Susan a text message yesterday.

components.note: 人 (person) — one person following another: 从 means to follow, then "from".
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 他从中得到了很多经验。
example.pinyin: tā cóngzhōng dédào le hěn duō jīngyàn.
example.english: He gained a lot of experience from it.
example.fact: After the near-catastrophic Apollo 13 mission in 1970, NASA engineers spent months analyzing exactly what had gone wrong with the oxygen tank. The lessons learned directly shaped safety redesigns used in every subsequent Apollo mission.

examples.hanzi: 这里有三本书，你可以从中选一本。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ yǒu sān běn shū, nǐ kěyǐ cóngzhōng xuǎn yì běn.
examples.english: There are three books here; you can choose one of them.

examples.hanzi: 他想从中找出一条更好的路。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng cóngzhōng zhǎo chū yì tiáo gèng hǎo de lù.
examples.english: He wants to find a better way from among these.

components.note: 爫 (hand, claw) — a hand pressing down; the traditional account is a hand calming a woman, so 'settled, secure'. Treat as a memory aid.
女 (woman) — a family also in 好 good, 妈 mum, 姓 surname; here the person being settled. Used in 妥当 proper, 妥协 compromise.

example.hanzi: 这个办法很妥当。
example.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ hěn tuǒdang.
example.english: This method is very suitable.
example.fact: 妥 gives 妥当 (proper), 妥协 (compromise), 妥善 (appropriate), 稳妥 (safe). 办妥 means to have settled something.

examples.hanzi: 这件事我们已经处理妥当了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒmen yǐjīng chǔlǐ tuǒdàng le.
examples.english: We have already handled this matter properly.

examples.hanzi: 机票都订妥了，你放心吧。
examples.pinyin: Jīpiào dōu dìng tuǒ le, nǐ fàngxīn ba.
examples.english: The flight tickets are all booked, so don't worry.

components.note: 父 (father) — marks the father, as in 爸 dad, 爷 grandfather; 爹 is dad.
多 (duō) is only a loose hint for diē.

example.hanzi: 我爹今年六十岁了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ diē jīnnián liùshí suì le.
example.english: My dad is sixty this year.
example.fact: 爹 is a colloquial, often dialect word for 'dad', and 爸 is the standard form. 爹妈 means 'mum and dad', and 坑爹 is slang for something outrageous.

examples.hanzi: 我爹每天早上去田里干活。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ diē měitiān zǎoshang qù tián lǐ gànhuó.
examples.english: My dad goes to work in the fields every morning.

examples.hanzi: 孩子大声喊着爹，跑了过去。
examples.pinyin: Háizi dàshēng hǎn zhe diē, pǎo le guòqù.
examples.english: The child ran over, shouting "Dad".

components.note: 重 (zhòng) is a sound clue for 种 zhǒng/zhòng; it means heavy (zhòng) or to repeat (chóng, as in 重新).
里 (village, unit) — the bottom; the dictionary takes it as the 'unit/measure' part, as in 重量 weight, 能量. 里 is also a Chinese mile.
旦 (dàn, dawn) — the top. A loose sound clue only today: liáng/liàng vs dàn. Do not rely on it.

example.hanzi: 这个包裹的重量超过了限制。
example.pinyin: zhège bāoguǒ de zhòngliàng chāoguò le xiànzhì.
example.english: This package's weight exceeds the limit.
example.fact: Until 2019, the kilogram was defined by a single platinum-iridium cylinder kept in a vault near Paris. Scientists then redefined it using the Planck constant, so weight standards no longer depend on one physical object that could theoretically be damaged.

examples.hanzi: 这个箱子的重量是二十公斤。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāngzi de zhòngliàng shì èrshí gōngjīn.
examples.english: The weight of this box is twenty kilograms.

examples.hanzi: 你知道这条鱼的重量吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhīdào zhè tiáo yú de zhòngliàng ma?
examples.english: Do you know how much this fish weighs?

components.note: 雨 (rain) — marks weather and moisture, as in 雪, 雷, 雾; 露 is dew.
路 (lù) gives the sound exactly: 露 lù (dew) or lòu (reveal).
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.hanzi: 他很久没有在公众场合露面了。
example.pinyin: tā hěn jiǔ méiyǒu zài gōngzhòng chǎnghé lòumiàn le.
example.english: He hasn't appeared in public for a long time.
example.fact: Billionaire Howard Hughes spent his final years almost entirely out of public view, reportedly going nearly a decade without being photographed. His disappearance fueled widespread rumors about his health and even his identity.

examples.hanzi: 明星只在酒会上露面了十分钟。
examples.pinyin: Míngxīng zhǐ zài jiǔhuì shàng lùmiàn le shí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: The star only made an appearance at the party for ten minutes.

examples.hanzi: 新郎一直没露面，大家都很着急。
examples.pinyin: Xīnláng yìzhí méi lùmiàn, dàjiā dōu hěn zháojí.
examples.english: The groom never showed up, and everyone was anxious.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks things to do with ground and soil, as in 地 ground, 坏 broken; 埋 is putting something into the earth.
里 (lǐ) — only a loose sound hint for mái today; mostly useful as the part that completes the shape.
艹 (grass) — 艹 here is grass over a body 死, with 廾 (two hands) laying it down — burial.

example.hanzi: 古埃及人会把法老埋葬在金字塔里。
example.pinyin: gǔ Āijí rén huì bǎ fǎlǎo máizàng zài jīnzìtǎ lǐ.
example.english: The ancient Egyptians would bury pharaohs inside pyramids.
example.fact: When archaeologist Howard Carter opened Tutankhamun's tomb in 1922, it was one of the only pharaonic burial sites found nearly intact. It contained over 5,000 artifacts, including the pharaoh's iconic solid-gold burial mask.

examples.hanzi: 这位老人被埋葬在家乡的山上。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎorén bèi máizàng zài jiāxiāng de shān shàng.
examples.english: The old man was buried on a hill in his hometown.

examples.hanzi: 战争结束后，人们埋葬了死者。
examples.pinyin: Zhànzhēng jiéshù hòu, rénmen máizàng le sǐzhě.
examples.english: After the war ended, people buried the dead.

components.note: 力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 怕, 忙, 情: a quick, glad heart.
夬 (guài) is a close sound clue for kuài; 夬 also in 块 kuài, 筷 kuài and 决 jué.

example.hanzi: 政府决定加快这项工程的进度。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ juédìng jiākuài zhè xiàng gōngchéng de jìndù.
example.english: The government decided to speed up the progress of this project.
example.fact: China's Fuxing bullet trains reach a commercial operating speed of 350 km/h, covering the roughly 1,300-kilometer trip from Beijing to Shanghai in under four and a half hours — a journey that once took over 30 hours by conventional rail.

examples.hanzi: 我们要加快脚步，不然赶不上车。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào jiākuài jiǎobù, bùrán gǎn bu shàng chē.
examples.english: We need to quicken our pace, or we'll miss the bus.

examples.hanzi: 请加快速度，我们要迟到了。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jiākuài sùdù, wǒmen yào chídào le.
examples.english: Please speed up; we're going to be late.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — often added to characters that only imitate foreign sounds, as in 啡 and 吗.
加 (jiā) gives a rough sound for kā — 咖 only imitates the sound of "coffee" and has no meaning of its own.
口 (mouth) — marks a character used for a drinkable or spoken sound; here it only helps spell "coffee" (咖啡).
非 (fēi) sounds exactly like 啡; the same clue is in 菲 fēi and 匪 fěi.
广 (building, shelter) — houses and shops: 床, 库, 座; 店 is a shop.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound hint; same part in 站 zhàn and 战 zhàn.

example.hanzi: 我们在咖啡店里聊了一个下午。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zài kāfēidiàn lǐ liáo le yí ge xiàwǔ.
example.english: We chatted in the coffee shop for a whole afternoon.
example.fact: Coffee is believed to have been discovered in Ethiopia, where legend credits a goatherd named Kaldi who noticed his goats becoming unusually energetic after eating berries from a certain tree. The practice of brewing coffee later spread through Yemen and the wider Islamic world by the 15th century.

examples.hanzi: 这家咖啡店的蛋糕很好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā kāfēidiàn de dàngāo hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: The cakes at this café are very tasty.

examples.hanzi: 我每天早上在咖啡店买一杯拿铁。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang zài kāfēidiàn mǎi yì bēi nátiě.
examples.english: Every morning I buy a latte at the café.

components.note: 止 (foot) — two footprints, one above the other, make a step; the same 止 is in 走 walk and 跑 run.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.hanzi: 从这里步行到火车站只要十分钟。
example.pinyin: cóng zhèlǐ bùxíng dào huǒchēzhàn zhǐ yào shí fēnzhōng.
example.english: It only takes ten minutes to walk from here to the train station.
example.fact: The longest unbroken walk on record was completed by George Meegan, who walked roughly 30,000 kilometers from the southern tip of South America to the northern edge of Alaska between 1977 and 1983 — a journey of nearly six and a half years.

examples.hanzi: 周末我喜欢步行去公园。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ xǐhuan bùxíng qù gōngyuán.
examples.english: On weekends I like to walk to the park.

examples.hanzi: 这条街只允许步行，不能开车。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo jiē zhǐ yǔnxǔ bùxíng, bù néng kāichē.
examples.english: This street is pedestrian only; cars are not allowed.

components.note: 化 (huà) — near sound — 华 is huá; 化 also changes tone to sound out 华.
十 (ten) — the bottom 十 is a simplified remnant; 华 is flowery and splendid, as in 中华.
丽 (beautiful) — simplified 麗, which showed a deer 鹿 with antlers, a symbol of grace. Seen in 美丽.

example.hanzi: 这座宫殿的装饰非常华丽。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò gōngdiàn de zhuāngshì fēicháng huálì.
example.english: This palace's decoration is extremely gorgeous.
example.fact: The Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles contains 357 mirrors and took roughly six years to complete in the late 17th century. It later became the site where the treaty ending World War I was signed, in 1919.

examples.hanzi: 她穿着一件华丽的晚礼服。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yí jiàn huálì de wǎnlǐfú.
examples.english: She wore a gorgeous evening gown.

examples.hanzi: 这家酒店的大堂十分华丽。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn de dàtáng shífēn huálì.
examples.english: The lobby of this hotel is very magnificent.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth and clothing, as in 布 cloth, 带 belt, 帽 hat; 常 first meant a long skirt (裳 cháng).
尚 (shàng) is a loose sound clue for cháng; 尚 also sounds out 堂 táng and 掌 zhǎng.
见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.

example.hanzi: 感冒是一种很常见的疾病。
example.pinyin: gǎnmào shì yì zhǒng hěn chángjiàn de jíbìng.
example.english: The common cold is a very common illness.
example.fact: More than 200 different virus strains, most commonly rhinoviruses, can cause the common cold. That genetic diversity is one reason a single universal vaccine against it has never been developed despite decades of research.

examples.hanzi: 在中国，这是一个很常见的名字。
examples.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó, zhè shì yí gè hěn chángjiàn de míngzi.
examples.english: In China, this is a very common name.

examples.hanzi: 这种小鸟在公园里很常见。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng xiǎo niǎo zài gōngyuán lǐ hěn chángjiàn.
examples.english: This kind of small bird is common in the park.

components.note: 火 (fire) — marks burning and heat, as in 燃, 灯, 热; 烧 is to burn or cook.
尧 (yáo) is a loose hint for shāo; 浇 jiāo and 晓 xiǎo share it.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: a person hurt. The traditional 傷 took its sound from 昜 yáng (also in 汤 and 场).

example.hanzi: 他在事故中受到了严重的烧伤。
example.pinyin: tā zài shìgù zhōng shòudào le yánzhòng de shāoshāng.
example.english: He suffered severe burns in the accident.
example.fact: Surgeons have used skin grafts to treat severe burns since at least the 19th century. Modern burn units can now grow sheets of a patient's own skin cells in a lab from a postage-stamp-sized sample within about two to three weeks for grafting onto large wounds.

examples.hanzi: 孩子被热水烧伤了手。
examples.pinyin: Háizi bèi rèshuǐ shāoshāng le shǒu.
examples.english: The child burned his hand with hot water.

examples.hanzi: 这种药膏可以治疗轻微的烧伤。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yàogāo kěyǐ zhìliáo qīngwēi de shāoshāng.
examples.english: This ointment can treat minor burns.

meanings: You are welcome to do whatever you like!

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and asking: 说, 谢, 谈; 请 is to ask politely.
青 (qīng) sounds like 请 (tone differs); same part in 清, 情, 晴, 精, 静.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do. 便 is a person adjusting things 更 to make them convenient (traditional explanation).

example.hanzi: 如果你想先走，请便。
example.pinyin: rúguǒ nǐ xiǎng xiān zǒu, qǐng biàn.
example.english: If you want to leave first, please go ahead.
example.fact: The economic term laissez-faire, French for 'let (them) do,' originated in 18th-century France when physiocrat economists argued that government should let markets operate without interference — a principle later cited by economists from Adam Smith onward.

examples.hanzi: 你累了就先回去休息，请便。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ lèi le jiù xiān huíqù xiūxi, qǐngbiàn.
examples.english: If you're tired, go back and rest first; as you wish.

examples.hanzi: 这些点心大家请便，别客气。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē diǎnxin dàjiā qǐngbiàn, bié kèqi.
examples.english: Help yourselves to these snacks, don't be shy.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 巾 is a cloth radical, as in 帽 hat, 带 belt; 布 is cloth, and by extension to spread or announce, as in 宣布.
丁 (dīng) — a nail seen from above; as a part it sounds out 钉 dīng, 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng, 灯 dēng.

example.hanzi: 他最喜欢吃巧克力布丁。
example.pinyin: tā zuì xǐhuān chī qiǎokèlì bùdīng.
example.english: He loves eating chocolate pudding most of all.
example.fact: The word pudding originally referred to savory dishes, like sausage encased in an animal's stomach, in medieval England. Sweet, dessert-style puddings only became the dominant meaning of the word in the 18th and 19th centuries.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的焦糖布丁特别好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de jiāotáng bùdīng tèbié hǎochī.
examples.english: The caramel pudding at this shop is especially delicious.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈用牛奶和鸡蛋做了布丁。
examples.pinyin: Māma yòng niúnǎi hé jīdàn zuò le bùdīng.
examples.english: Mom made pudding with milk and eggs.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
口 (mouth) — marks speaking, shouting, eating and sounds, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 喊 is to shout.
咸 (xián) — sound hint is loose now (hǎn vs xián); same part sits in 减 jiǎn and 感 gǎn.
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
口 (mouth) — calling and speech: 吗, 喊, 呼; 叫 is to shout.
丩 (jiū) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 纠 jiū.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在操场上大喊大叫地跑来跑去。
example.pinyin: háizimen zài cāochǎng shàng dàhǎndàjiào de pǎo lái pǎo qù.
example.english: The children ran around the playground shouting and screaming.
example.fact: The Guinness World Record for the loudest human scream is held by Jill Drake of the UK, who reached 129 decibels in 2023 — roughly comparable to standing near a jet engine at takeoff.

examples.hanzi: 别在图书馆里大喊大叫。
examples.pinyin: Bié zài túshūguǎn lǐ dàhǎn-dàjiào.
examples.english: Don't shout and yell in the library.

examples.hanzi: 他生气地对着电话大喊大叫。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēngqì de duìzhe diànhuà dàhǎn-dàjiào.
examples.english: He angrily yelled into the phone.

components.note: 石 (stone) — marks stones and minerals, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break; magnets were first known as lodestone.
兹 (zī) — gives the sound, cí vs zī; 兹 also sounds out 滋 zī.
巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 帽, 帮: a belt of cloth with pieces hanging from it.

example.hanzi: 这些老歌都保存在磁带里。
example.pinyin: zhèxiē lǎo gē dōu bǎocún zài cídài lǐ.
example.english: These old songs are all stored on cassette tape.
example.fact: Magnetic tape recording was pioneered in Germany in the 1930s with the Magnetophon. The format later became the backbone of both music cassettes and, for decades, the primary medium for storing digital computer data before affordable hard drives took over.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷还保存着一盒旧磁带。
examples.pinyin: Yéye hái bǎocún zhe yì hé jiù cídài.
examples.english: Grandpa still keeps a box of old cassette tapes.

examples.hanzi: 这盘磁带已经放了三十年了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè pán cídài yǐjīng fàng le sānshí nián le.
examples.english: This tape has been played for thirty years.

components.note: 卜 (divination) — cracks read on heated bones; 口 below is asking. 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: to grip or rely on.
居 (jū) is a close sound clue for jù; 居 also in 剧 jù and 锯 jù.

example.hanzi: 智能手机占据了我们大部分的空闲时间。
example.pinyin: zhìnéng shǒujī zhànjù le wǒmen dàbùfèn de kòngxián shíjiān.
example.english: Smartphones occupy most of our free time.
example.fact: Global surveys report that the average smartphone user now spends over four hours a day on their device, a figure that has roughly doubled over the past decade as mobile internet access and app usage have expanded.

examples.hanzi: 大树占据了院子的一半。
examples.pinyin: Dà shù zhànjù le yuànzi de yíbàn.
examples.english: The big tree takes up half of the yard.

examples.hanzi: 他占据了领先位置，一直没有被超过。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhànjù le lǐngxiān wèizhi, yìzhí méiyǒu bèi chāoguò.
examples.english: He took the leading position and was never overtaken.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 稳 is firm, steady, like a solid harvest.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).

example.hanzi: 大家保持冷静，先稳住局势。
example.pinyin: dàjiā bǎochí lěngjìng, xiān wěnzhù júshì.
example.english: Everyone stay calm, let's stabilize the situation first.
example.fact: Modern rockets and satellites use spinning gyroscopes or reaction wheels to stay stable in orientation. The same principle keeps a spinning bicycle wheel resistant to tipping over, a phenomenon studied in physics since the 19th century.

examples.hanzi: 你先稳住，别着急，慢慢说。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān wěnzhù, bié zháojí, mànmàn shuō.
examples.english: Calm down first, don't rush, and speak slowly.

examples.hanzi: 他用手稳住梯子，让我爬上去。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng shǒu wěnzhù tīzi, ràng wǒ pá shàngqù.
examples.english: He held the ladder steady so I could climb up.

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — 纟 is the simplified 糸 (silk); 丝 is the simplified form of 絲, two skeins of silk side by side.
毛 (hair, fur) — hair and fine things: 毯 blanket, 尾 tail; 毫 is fine hair, then a tiny amount, as in 毫米 millimeter.
高 (gāo) is only a loose sound hint for háo.

example.hanzi: 他丝毫没有感到害怕。
example.pinyin: tā sīháo méiyǒu gǎndào hàipà.
example.english: He didn't feel afraid in the slightest.
example.fact: The gravitational-wave detector LIGO can measure distance changes smaller than one ten-thousandth the width of a proton. That almost unimaginably tiny precision let scientists confirm ripples in spacetime that Einstein had predicted a century earlier.

examples.hanzi: 别怕，我丝毫没有怪你的意思。
examples.pinyin: Bié pà, wǒ sīháo méiyǒu guài nǐ de yìsi.
examples.english: Don't worry, I don't blame you in the slightest.

examples.hanzi: 这件事丝毫不会影响我们的计划。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì sīháo bú huì yǐngxiǎng wǒmen de jìhuà.
examples.english: This will not affect our plan in the least.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread; traditional 糸) — marks thread, cloth and binding, as in 红 red, 给 give; 综 is arranging threads for weaving, then combining.
宗 (zōng) — same sound: 综 zōng. 宗 also sounds out 踪 zōng and 棕 zōng.
合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.
疒 (illness) — 疒 is the sickness radical, as in 病, 痛, 痕; 症 is an illness or its symptoms.
正 (zhèng) — same sound — 症 is zhèng, like 正; 正 also sounds out 证 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 医生诊断他患有代谢综合症。
example.pinyin: yīshēng zhěnduàn tā huàn yǒu dàixiè zōnghézhèng.
example.english: The doctor diagnosed him with metabolic syndrome.
example.fact: The term Stockholm syndrome was coined after a 1973 bank robbery in Stockholm, Sweden, during which hostages held for six days developed sympathetic feelings toward their captors. Criminologists have since studied the same response in other hostage situations.

examples.hanzi: 这种综合症在儿童中很少见。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng zōnghézhèng zài értóng zhōng hěn shǎojiàn.
examples.english: This syndrome is rare among children.

examples.hanzi: 医生解释了什么是唐氏综合症。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng jiěshì le shénme shì Tángshì zōnghézhèng.
examples.english: The doctor explained what Down syndrome is.

components.note: 木 (wood, tree) — wood radical — 格 first meant a wooden frame or lattice, hence "pattern, standard"; compare 树 tree, 板 board.
各 (gè) — same syllable, different tone — 格 is gé; 各 also sounds out 阁 gé and 胳 gē.
木 (tree) — two trees side by side make a grove or forest; compare 森 with three.

example.hanzi: 格林先生是这所学校的校长。
example.pinyin: Gélín xiānsheng shì zhè suǒ xuéxiào de xiàozhǎng.
example.english: Mr. Green is the principal of this school.
example.fact: Green is among the ten most common surnames in England, originally an occupational or descriptive nickname for someone who lived near a village green or who often wore green clothing in the Middle Ages.

examples.hanzi: 格林是一位很有名的园艺师。
examples.pinyin: Gélín shì yí wèi hěn yǒumíng de yuányìshī.
examples.english: Green is a very famous gardener.

examples.hanzi: 我和格林在公司门口见了面。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé Gélín zài gōngsī ménkǒu jiàn le miàn.
examples.english: I met Green at the company entrance.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 火 is fire, as in 烧, 灯, 炒; 烟 is smoke.
因 (yīn) — near sound — 烟 is yān; 因 also sounds out 姻 yīn.
雨 (rain) — marks weather and moisture, as in 雪 snow, 雷 thunder, 露 dew; fog is water hanging in the air.
务 (wù) — same sound: 雾 wù. 务 also appears in 误 wù.

example.hanzi: 浓浓的烟雾笼罩着整个城市。
example.pinyin: nóngnóng de yānwù lóngzhào zhe zhěnggè chéngshì.
example.english: Thick smog blanketed the entire city.
example.fact: The Great Smog of London in December 1952 trapped a thick layer of coal-smoke pollution over the city for five days and is estimated to have caused several thousand deaths. It directly led to the UK's Clean Air Act of 1956.

examples.hanzi: 篝火冒出的烟雾让人睁不开眼睛。
examples.pinyin: Gōuhuǒ màochū de yānwù ràng rén zhēng bu kāi yǎnjing.
examples.english: The smoke from the campfire made it hard to open one's eyes.

examples.hanzi: 山谷里的烟雾慢慢散开了。
examples.pinyin: Shāngǔ lǐ de yānwù mànmàn sànkāi le.
examples.english: The smoke in the valley slowly cleared away.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks soil and ground, as in 地 ground, 城 city wall, 坏 broken; 塌 is collapsing, as in 倒塌.

example.hanzi: 房子被大雪压塌了。
example.pinyin: Fángzi bèi dàxuě yā tā le.
example.english: The house collapsed under the heavy snow.
example.fact: 塌 gives 倒塌 (collapse), 塌方 (landslide), 塌陷 (cave-in) and 塌实 (at ease, also written 踏实). 塌房 became slang for a celebrity's reputation collapsing.

examples.hanzi: 大雨过后，墙塌了。
examples.pinyin: Dàyǔ guòhòu, qiáng tā le.
examples.english: After the heavy rain, the wall collapsed.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的蛋糕塌下去了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de dàngāo tā xiàqù le.
examples.english: The cake from this shop sank in the middle.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — marks the head and face, as in 顶, 题, 顺; 预 is thinking ahead.
予 (yǔ) hints at the sound: 预 yù is close, as in 豫 yù.

example.hanzi: 我想提前预订一个房间。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng tíqián yùdìng yí gè fángjiān.
example.english: I'd like to reserve a room in advance.
example.fact: 预 gives 预订 (book), 预习 (prepare lessons), 预报 (forecast), 预防 (prevent), 预算 (budget).

examples.hanzi: 你们预订了几个房间？
examples.pinyin: Nǐmen yùdìng le jǐ ge fángjiān?
examples.english: How many rooms did you reserve?

examples.hanzi: 明天的天气预报说有大雨。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān de tiānqì yùbào shuō yǒu dàyǔ.
examples.english: Tomorrow's weather forecast says there will be heavy rain.

components.note: 王 (jade; 玉) — marks jewels and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 珠 pearl; 瑜 is a fine jade, as in 瑜伽 yoga.
俞 (yú) — same sound: 瑜 yú. 俞 also sounds out 愉 yú and 逾 yú.

example.hanzi: 我周末去上瑜伽课。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò qù shàng yújiā kè.
example.english: I go to a yoga class on weekends.
example.fact: 瑜 originally means beautiful jade: 瑕不掩瑜 ('a flaw doesn't hide the jade's luster'). It's also in 瑜伽 (yoga) and in names such as 周瑜.

examples.hanzi: 她每周去练两次瑜伽。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi zhōu qù liàn liǎng cì yújiā.
examples.english: She goes to practice yoga twice a week.

examples.hanzi: 这位老师教瑜伽教得特别好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎoshī jiāo yújiā jiāo de tèbié hǎo.
examples.english: This teacher teaches yoga especially well.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — marks hills and heights, as in 岛 island, 峰 peak; 岗 first meant a ridge, later a post to stand guard on.
冈 (gāng) — close sound: 岗 gǎng. 冈 also sounds out 钢 gāng and 刚 gāng.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住.
立 (stand) — the spot where a person 亻 stands 立: a position or seat; also 位置 position.

example.hanzi: 每个员工都要坚守自己的岗位。
example.pinyin: měi ge yuángōng dōu yào jiānshǒu zìjǐ de gǎngwèi.
example.english: Every employee must stay firm at their post.
example.fact: Before automation, lighthouse keepers held one of the most isolated jobs in the world, sometimes staying at remote posts for months at a time to keep the light burning. Most countries had fully automated their lighthouses by the late 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 他在这个岗位上工作了十年。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhège gǎngwèi shàng gōngzuò le shí nián.
examples.english: He has worked in this post for ten years.

examples.hanzi: 公司正在招聘新的销售岗位。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī zhèngzài zhāopìn xīn de xiāoshòu gǎngwèi.
examples.english: The company is hiring for new sales positions.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.

example.hanzi: 诚实是建立信任的前提。
example.pinyin: chéngshí shì jiànlì xìnrèn de qiántí.
example.english: Honesty is the precondition for building trust.
example.fact: Euclid's Elements, written around 300 BC, built the entire foundation of geometry from just five basic premises, or axioms. That method of reasoning from a small set of assumptions to derive complex results became a model for mathematics and logic for over two thousand years.

examples.hanzi: 没有这个前提，一切都无从谈起。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu zhège qiántí, yíqiè dōu wúcóng tánqǐ.
examples.english: Without this precondition, nothing can even be discussed.

examples.hanzi: 在这个前提下，我们可以继续谈。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhège qiántí xià, wǒmen kěyǐ jìxù tán.
examples.english: Under this premise, we can continue talking.

components.note: 日 (sun) — marks light and warmth, as in 晴, 暗, 暖; 暖 is sunny warmth.
爰 (yuán) is a loose hint for nuǎn; 缓 huǎn and 援 yuán share it.
口 (mouth) — 口 is the mouth, as in 吃, 喝, 叫; 和 is harmony and speaking together.
禾 (hé) — same sound — 和 is hé, like 禾.

example.hanzi: 今天太阳出来了，暖和多了。
example.pinyin: jīntiān tàiyáng chūlái le, nuǎnhuo duō le.
example.english: The sun came out today, so it's much warmer.
example.fact: Iceland heats roughly 90% of its homes using geothermal energy piped directly from underground hot springs, taking advantage of the same volcanic activity that produces the country's famous outdoor thermal pools.

examples.hanzi: 进了屋子，大家觉得很暖和。
examples.pinyin: Jìn le wūzi, dàjiā juéde hěn nuǎnhuo.
examples.english: After going into the house, everyone felt warm.

examples.hanzi: 多穿点衣服，暖和一些。
examples.pinyin: Duō chuān diǎn yīfu, nuǎnhuo yìxiē.
examples.english: Wear more clothes to keep warm.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 住 live.
旦 (dàn) gives the exact sound; 旦 also sounds out 担 dān and 胆 dǎn.

example.hanzi: 他不但聪明，而且非常勤奋。
example.pinyin: tā bùdàn cōngming, érqiě fēicháng qínfèn.
example.english: He is not only smart, but also very hardworking.
example.fact: Marie Curie is not only the first woman to win a Nobel Prize but also the only person in history to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences — physics in 1903 and chemistry in 1911.

examples.hanzi: 他不但会说英语，还会说法语。
examples.pinyin: Tā búdàn huì shuō Yīngyǔ, hái huì shuō Fǎyǔ.
examples.english: Not only can he speak English, he can speak French too.

examples.hanzi: 这家饭店不但便宜，而且很干净。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā fàndiàn búdàn piányi, érqiě hěn gānjìng.
examples.english: This restaurant is not only cheap but also clean.

components.note: 米 (rice, grain) — 米 is rice and grain, as in 粥, 糖, 精; 粉 is flour ground from grain, then powder.
分 (fēn) — same sound, different tone — 粉 is fěn; 分 also sounds out 份 fèn.
纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸 (silk); colours came from dyed silk, as in 绿, 紫, 给.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 红 is hóng; 工 also sounds out 江 jiāng and 空 kōng.

example.hanzi: 她穿着一条粉红色的裙子。
example.pinyin: tā chuānzhe yì tiáo fěnhóngsè de qúnzi.
example.english: She was wearing a pink skirt.
example.fact: Flamingos are born with gray feathers and only turn pink because of pigments called carotenoids in the algae and crustaceans they eat. Flamingos raised on a diet lacking these pigments, as in some zoos, can remain pale or white.

examples.hanzi: 粉红色的花开满了整个院子。
examples.pinyin: Fěnhóngsè de huā kāi mǎn le zhěnggè yuànzi.
examples.english: Pink flowers filled the whole yard.

examples.hanzi: 小女孩的脸蛋被冻得粉红。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo nǚhái de liǎndàn bèi dòng de fěnhóng.
examples.english: The little girl's cheeks were frozen pink.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 迷 is losing one's way.
米 (mǐ) — near sound — 迷 is mí, the same syllable with a different tone.
心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 爱; 恋 is to love or long for.
The sound part is traditional 戀 (luán), replaced in 恋 by 亦 (yì) only for simplicity — a loose clue for liàn.

example.hanzi: 他从小就迷恋赛车运动。
example.pinyin: tā cóngxiǎo jiù míliàn sàichē yùndòng.
example.english: He has been infatuated with car racing since childhood.
example.fact: During the Dutch 'tulip mania' of the 1630s, buyers became so infatuated with rare tulip bulbs that a single bulb could sell for more than a skilled craftsman earned in a decade — before the market collapsed almost overnight in 1637.

examples.hanzi: 她从小就迷恋画画，每天都画。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù míliàn huàhuà, měi tiān dōu huà.
examples.english: She has been devoted to drawing since childhood and draws every day.

examples.hanzi: 他现在迷恋上了网络游戏。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiànzài míliàn shàng le wǎngluò yóuxì.
examples.english: He is now hooked on online games.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.
彳 (step) — marks walking, as in 行, 往, 很, 得; 徒 pairs it with 走 walk: going on foot, then a follower.
走 (walk) — as in 跑 run, 起 rise.

example.hanzi: 很多信徒每年都会去麦加朝圣。
example.pinyin: hěn duō xìntú měi nián dōu huì qù Màijiā cháoshèng.
example.english: Many believers make the pilgrimage to Mecca every year.
example.fact: The annual Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca draws roughly two million Muslim believers from around the world each year, making it one of the largest peaceful gatherings of people on Earth.

examples.hanzi: 信徒们每周日都去教堂做礼拜。
examples.pinyin: Xìntúmen měi zhōu rì dōu qù jiàotáng zuò lǐbài.
examples.english: The believers go to church every Sunday for worship.

examples.hanzi: 这位僧人有很多信徒。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi sēngrén yǒu hěn duō xìntú.
examples.english: This monk has many followers.

components.note: 止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 别闲聊了，咱们说点正事。
example.pinyin: bié xiánliáo le, zánmen shuō diǎn zhèngshì.
example.english: Stop chit-chatting, let's talk about something important.
example.fact: The Pomodoro Technique, developed in the late 1980s by Francesco Cirillo, uses a kitchen timer shaped like a tomato (pomodoro in Italian) to break work into focused 25-minute intervals — a simple method still widely used today to stay on task.

examples.hanzi: 先别玩了，我们谈正事吧。
examples.pinyin: Xiān bié wán le, wǒmen tán zhèngshì ba.
examples.english: Stop playing for now; let's talk business.

examples.hanzi: 他整天不干正事，只知道玩。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhěngtiān bú gàn zhèngshì, zhǐ zhīdào wán.
examples.english: He doesn't do anything useful all day and only knows how to play.

components.note: 目 (eye) — the top part is a stacked eye 罒; 睾 is a variant of 睪, the part in 译 yì, 泽 zé, 择 zé, 释 shì; sound clue is loose and the meaning sense is modern.
幸 (luck) — the lower part, with no useful meaning link. Only used in 睾丸; learn it as a fixed word.
丸 (ball, pill) — a small round thing; the shape is a tiny bent figure, now just remember it as a pellet or pill, as in 药丸 pill.

example.hanzi: 这项检查是为了排查睾丸方面的疾病。
example.pinyin: zhè xiàng jiǎnchá shì wèile páichá gāowán fāngmiàn de jíbìng.
example.english: This exam is meant to screen for testicular conditions.
example.fact: Human testes hang outside the body cavity because sperm production requires a temperature slightly cooler than the core body temperature, roughly 2 to 4 degrees Celsius lower. Muscles in the scrotum draw the testes closer to or farther from the body to regulate this temperature.

examples.hanzi: 医生建议他去检查睾丸。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì tā qù jiǎnchá gāowán.
examples.english: The doctor advised him to have his testicles examined.

examples.hanzi: 睾丸是男性重要的生殖器官。
examples.pinyin: Gāowán shì nánxìng zhòngyào de shēngzhí qìguān.
examples.english: The testicles are an important male reproductive organ.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — a hand 又 taking an ear 耳: in ancient battle a trophy of capture. Seen in 取得 and in 娶 qǔ, 趣 qù, 最 zuì.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 医生小心地把弹片从伤口里取出。
example.pinyin: yīshēng xiǎoxīn de bǎ dànpiàn cóng shāngkǒu lǐ qǔchū.
example.english: The doctor carefully removed the shrapnel from the wound.
example.fact: The world's first cash-dispensing ATM was installed by Barclays Bank in London in 1967. The inventor reportedly tested it with a cheque cashed for a fictional sum, and the machine could dispense at most £10 per transaction.

examples.hanzi: 他从口袋里取出一把钥匙。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng kǒudài lǐ qǔchū yì bǎ yàoshi.
examples.english: He took a key out of his pocket.

examples.hanzi: 请把手机里的卡取出来。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shǒujī lǐ de kǎ qǔ chūlái.
examples.english: Please take the card out of the phone.

components.note: 页 (page, head) — marks things to do with the head or face, as in 顺, 领 lead; 颁 is bestowing and issuing publicly.
分 (fēn) — sound hint is loose now (bān vs fēn); 分 also hints at dividing out awards, as in 颁奖.
将 (jiāng) is the trimmed top part: 奖 jiǎng sounds like 桨 jiǎng and 浆 jiāng.

example.hanzi: 颁奖仪式将在下周举行。
example.pinyin: bānjiǎng yíshì jiāng zài xià zhōu jǔxíng.
example.english: The award ceremony will be held next week.
example.fact: The Academy Award statuette, nicknamed 'Oscar,' is made of gold-plated britannium and stands 13.5 inches tall. The earliest statuettes, first awarded in 1929, were solid bronze and only gold-plated from the 1930s onward.

examples.hanzi: 学校会给优秀学生颁奖。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào huì gěi yōuxiù xuésheng bānjiǎng.
examples.english: The school will present awards to outstanding students.

examples.hanzi: 市长亲自来为冠军颁奖。
examples.pinyin: Shìzhǎng qīnzì lái wèi guànjūn bānjiǎng.
examples.english: The mayor came in person to present the champion's award.

meanings: variant of 答覆|答复[da2 fu4]

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — written things and bamboo goods: 笔 pen, 第 order, 筷 chopsticks; 答 comes from bamboo slips used for replies.
合 (hé, together) — matching an answer to a question; sound is only loose, but 合 also sounds out 搭 dā.
复 (fù) sounds out 腹 fù belly and 覆 fù cover; as a word it means again or to repeat, as in 恢复, 重复.

example.hanzi: 公司已经对客户的投诉做出了答复。
example.pinyin: gōngsī yǐjīng duì kèhù de tóusù zuò chū le dáfù.
example.english: The company has already responded to the customer's complaint.
example.fact: In 2018, a message in a bottle thrown from a German research ship in 1886 was found on an Australian beach, still carrying its original reply card. At 132 years, it became the oldest message in a bottle ever recovered — finally answered more than a century later.

examples.hanzi: 我会在三天内给你答复。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì zài sān tiān nèi gěi nǐ dáfù.
examples.english: I will give you a reply within three days.

examples.hanzi: 请尽快答复我，我好安排时间。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jǐnkuài dáfù wǒ, wǒ hǎo ānpái shíjiān.
examples.english: Please reply to me soon so I can arrange my time.

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk, as in 说, 话, 谎; 诡 is sly, deceitful talk.
危 (wēi) is a loose hint for guǐ; 跪 guì shares it.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; counting aloud.
十 (ten) — counting up to ten: 计 is to count and reckon.

example.hanzi: 敌人的诡计被我们及时发现了。
example.pinyin: dírén de guǐjì bèi wǒmen jíshí fāxiàn le.
example.english: We discovered the enemy's trick in time.
example.fact: The legendary Trojan Horse, described in Homer's Iliad and Virgil's Aeneid, tells of Greek soldiers hiding inside a giant wooden horse to trick their way into the city of Troy. The story is the origin of the modern term 'Trojan horse' used for deceptive computer malware.

examples.hanzi: 这是一个骗人的诡计，千万别上当。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè piàn rén de guǐjì, qiānwàn bié shàngdàng.
examples.english: This is a trick to cheat people; don't fall for it.

examples.hanzi: 他用了一个小诡计让对手犯错。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng le yí gè xiǎo guǐjì ràng duìshǒu fàncuò.
examples.english: He used a little trick to make his opponent err.

components.note: 虍 (tiger stripes) — the tiger family: 虎 tiger, 虚 empty, 处 place. A tiger awe may suggest 'devout', but that is a guess.
文 (writing, culture) — the lower part. Memory aid: devout people honour ritual and writing (文) with the awe one has for a tiger.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 请; 诚 is honest speech.
成 (chéng) — same sound — 诚 is chéng, like 成; 成 also sounds out 城 chéng.

example.hanzi: 他是一个非常虔诚的教徒。
example.pinyin: tā shì yí ge fēicháng qiánchéng de jiàotú.
example.english: He is a very devout believer.
example.fact: Mount Athos in Greece has been home to Eastern Orthodox monks for over a thousand years and remains one of the strictest religious communities in the world — women have been barred from setting foot on the peninsula since at least the 9th century.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶虔诚地向佛像拜了三拜。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai qiánchéng de xiàng fóxiàng bài le sān bài.
examples.english: Grandma devoutly bowed three times to the Buddha statue.

examples.hanzi: 他用虔诚的态度对待这份工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng qiánchéng de tàidù duìdài zhè fèn gōngzuò.
examples.english: He treats this job with devotion.

components.note: 木 — a tree with trunk, branches and roots; the wood radical, as in 林 forest, 树 tree, 桌 table.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 偶 first meant a figure or doll, then a pair.
禺 (yú) is a loose sound clue; same part in 遇 yù, 愚 yú, 寓 yù.

example.hanzi: 这个木偶剧团来自捷克。
example.pinyin: zhège mù'ǒu jùtuán láizì Jiékè.
example.english: This puppet theater troupe is from the Czech Republic.
example.fact: Czech marionette puppetry is recognized by UNESCO as part of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The tradition dates back to the 19th century, when itinerant puppeteers performed folk tales and satire across Bohemia and Moravia.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在看木偶表演。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài kàn mù'ǒu biǎoyǎn.
examples.english: The children are watching a puppet show.

examples.hanzi: 老人用木头做了一个小木偶。
examples.pinyin: Lǎorén yòng mùtou zuò le yí gè xiǎo mù'ǒu.
examples.english: The old man made a little wooden puppet.

components.note: 参 (cān) is a sound clue for 惨 cǎn and 掺 chān; the old shape pictured three stars.
贝 (cowrie) — money and value, as in 财, 货, 买: competing for prizes was once tied to offerings and stakes.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 这次比赛共有五百名参赛者。
example.pinyin: zhè cì bǐsài gòng yǒu wǔbǎi míng cānsàizhě.
example.english: There are five hundred competitors in this competition in total.
example.fact: The New York City Marathon is one of the largest marathons in the world, with roughly 50,000 official finishers each year — more people than live in many small towns, all crossing the same finish line in Central Park.

examples.hanzi: 每位参赛者都拿到了一枚纪念章。
examples.pinyin: Měi wèi cānsàizhě dōu nádào le yì méi jìniànzhāng.
examples.english: Every contestant received a commemorative badge.

examples.hanzi: 参赛者要在八点前到达现场。
examples.pinyin: Cānsàizhě yào zài bā diǎn qián dàodá xiànchǎng.
examples.english: Contestants must arrive at the venue before eight o'clock.

components.note: 凶 (ominous) — an open pit 凵 with crossed marks inside: a trap, a sign of danger; seen in 凶手 murderer, 凶器 weapon.
乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌, 树, 板: 案 is a wooden table.
安 (ān) is a close sound clue for àn; also in 按 àn.

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查这起凶杀案。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá zhè qǐ xiōngshā'àn.
example.english: The police are investigating this murder case.
example.fact: DNA fingerprinting was developed by British geneticist Alec Jeffreys in 1984 after he noticed that certain DNA sequences varied enough between individuals to serve as a unique identifier. It was first used to solve a real crime in 1988, when it helped convict Colin Pitchfork of two murders in Leicestershire, England — the first criminal conviction secured through DNA evidence.

examples.hanzi: 这起凶杀案发生在昨天深夜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè qǐ xiōngshā'àn fāshēng zài zuótiān shēnyè.
examples.english: This murder case happened late last night.

examples.hanzi: 侦探接手了那桩凶杀案。
examples.pinyin: Zhēntàn jiēshǒu le nà zhuāng xiōngshā'àn.
examples.english: The detective took over that murder case.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes and barriers, as in 院, 阶, 障; 防 is a dike to guard against floods, then to defend.
方 (fāng) gives the sound: 防 fáng is close, as in 房 fáng and 妨 fáng.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: guarding with the hands.
户 (hù, door) gives the exact sound; 户 means door or household.

example.hanzi: 工人们戴上防护眼镜再开始操作机器。
example.pinyin: Gōngrénmen dàishàng fánghù yǎnjìng zài kāishǐ cāozuò jīqì.
example.english: The workers put on protective goggles before operating the machinery.
example.fact: Kevlar, now a staple of protective gear like bulletproof vests and cut-resistant gloves, was invented almost by accident in 1965 by DuPont chemist Stephanie Kwolek while she was researching lightweight fibers for tires. Weight for weight, it is about five times stronger than steel.

examples.hanzi: 骑自行车一定要戴好防护头盔。
examples.pinyin: Qí zìxíngchē yídìng yào dài hǎo fánghù tóukuī.
examples.english: You must wear a protective helmet when riding a bike.

examples.hanzi: 这种防护服可以挡住灰尘。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng fánghù fú kěyǐ dǎngzhù huīchén.
examples.english: This protective suit can keep out dust.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and plants, as in 树, 林, 村; 植 is to plant.
直 (zhí) gives the sound exactly: 植 zhí, also in 值 zhí and 殖 zhí.

example.hanzi: 春天我们一起植树。
example.pinyin: Chūntiān wǒmen yìqǐ zhíshù.
example.english: In spring we plant trees together.
example.fact: 植 gives 植物 (plant), 植树节 (Arbor Day, 12 March in China), 移植 (transplant) and 种植 (cultivate).

examples.hanzi: 他在阳台上种植了很多花。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yángtái shàng zhòngzhí le hěn duō huā.
examples.english: He grows a lot of flowers on the balcony.

examples.hanzi: 植物需要阳光和水。
examples.pinyin: Zhíwù xūyào yángguāng hé shuǐ.
examples.english: Plants need sunlight and water.

components.note: 疒 (illness) — marks wounds and ailments, as in 病 sick, 痛 pain; 疤 is a scar.
巴 (bā) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 吧 ba, 爸 bà and 芭 bā.

example.hanzi: 他脸上有一道疤。
example.pinyin: Tā liǎn shang yǒu yí dào bā.
example.english: He has a scar on his face.
example.fact: The measure word is 道: 一道疤. 伤疤 means scar, 揭伤疤 means 'to pick at an old wound', and 好了伤疤忘了疼 means to forget pain once healed.

examples.hanzi: 他手上有一个旧伤疤。
examples.pinyin: Tā shǒu shàng yǒu yí ge jiù shāngbā.
examples.english: He has an old scar on his hand.

examples.hanzi: 伤口好了以后会留下疤。
examples.pinyin: Shāngkǒu hǎo le yǐhòu huì liú xià bā.
examples.english: After the wound heals, a scar will remain.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and wooden things, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; 横 is a crossbar, then horizontal, as in 横线.
黄 (huáng) — loose sound hint (héng vs huáng).

example.hanzi: 他把箱子横着放。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ xiāngzi héng zhe fàng.
example.english: He placed the box sideways.
example.fact: 横 is the opposite of 竖. It's also the first stroke 一 in writing. 横 read hèng means fierce, as in 蛮横 (unreasonable).

examples.hanzi: 马路上有一条横线。
examples.pinyin: Mǎlù shàng yǒu yì tiáo héngxiàn.
examples.english: There is a horizontal line on the road.

examples.hanzi: 他横穿马路，很危险。
examples.pinyin: Tā héngchuān mǎlù, hěn wēixiǎn.
examples.english: He crossed the road diagonally, which is dangerous.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — marks feelings and mood, as in 怕 fear, 快 happy, 恨 hate; 懒 is lazy, a feeling of disinclination.
赖 (lài) — loose sound hint (lǎn vs lài); same part in 懒 lǎn and 癞 lài.

example.hanzi: 他很懒，不爱做家务。
example.pinyin: Tā hěn lǎn, bú ài zuò jiāwù.
example.english: He's lazy and dislikes housework.
example.fact: 懒 gives 偷懒 (slack off), 懒得 (can't be bothered: 懒得说), and 睡懒觉 (sleep in).

examples.hanzi: 你别太懒，要多运动。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié tài lǎn, yào duō yùndòng.
examples.english: Don't be too lazy, and exercise more.

examples.hanzi: 周末我就想懒在床上。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ jiù xiǎng lǎn zài chuáng shàng.
examples.english: On weekends I just want to laze in bed.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 激 is water surging up, then to stir up.
敫 (jiǎo) is only a loose sound clue for jī.

example.hanzi: 这个消息让大家很激动。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi ràng dàjiā hěn jīdòng.
example.english: This news got everyone excited.
example.fact: 激 gives 激动 (excited or moved), 刺激 (stimulate), 激烈 (fierce), 激光 (laser), 感激 (grateful). 激动 can be positive or angry.

examples.hanzi: 听到好消息，他很激动。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào hǎo xiāoxi, tā hěn jīdòng.
examples.english: Hearing the good news, he was very excited.

examples.hanzi: 比赛进行得很激烈。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài jìnxíng de hěn jīliè.
examples.english: The match was very intense.

components.note: 女 (woman) — marks women and family terms, as in 妈 mom, 姐 sister, 好 good; 妖 is a bewitching spirit, as in 妖怪 monster.
夭 (yāo) — same sound: 妖 yāo. 夭 also sounds out 沃 wò and 笑 xiào.

example.hanzi: 故事里有一只狐狸妖。
example.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ yǒu yì zhī húli yāo.
example.english: There's a fox demon in the story.
example.fact: 妖 gives 妖怪 (monster), 妖精 (spirit), and also means bewitching (妖艳). Folk tales about 狐妖 are classic.

examples.hanzi: 电影里有很多妖怪。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ yǒu hěn duō yāoguài.
examples.english: There are a lot of monsters in the movie.

examples.hanzi: 她穿得太妖艳了。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān de tài yāoyàn le.
examples.english: She is dressed too flashily.
